collapseRootCause: src/observer/layout-probe.ts:989 (pre-fix) — probeLayout's own page load called page.goto() and DISCARDED the response, so the main document's HTTP status was never read. page.goto does not throw on 4xx/5xx, so a transient upstream error body (text/plain, wrapped by Chrome in <pre>) was walked and recorded as a legitimate 3-element layout probe. The Task 28.7 B1 document gate (isOkStatus + navigateMainDocument + non-2xx retry + sourceIntegrity mark) already existed but was private to observe-page.ts and applied only to the DEEP observation's load; the pipeline makes four loads per URL and the probe's two got none of it.
collapseProvenance: PRE-EXISTING; trigger site-side and transient. NOT caused by this wave's three observer changes. Proof: the identical 3-element html/body/pre shape struck the DESKTOP DEEP observation of p000001 AND p000002 in run 2026-09-04T15-30-50-831Z — the 28.7 PRE-LANE run — where rendered.html preserves the body verbatim: 'upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. retried and the latest reset reason: remote connection failure'. The brief's stale-parked-list hypothesis is DISPROVEN by the artifact: disconnected==0 at all 16 widths and tags.length==3 (the collapse is in the WALK, before any resize), plus documentWidth 980 = Chrome's no-viewport-meta default.
alignmentRootCause: src/sitespec/compile-page.ts computeProbeAttachment (pre-fix) — probe-to-tree attachment was a LEADING INDEX PREFIX from 0, requiring tag AND parent-INDEX equality at every position. The probe is a separate page load, so one element-count difference in a dynamically-mounted subtree shifts every parent index after it and terminates attachment. Measured on linear.app / mobile (healthy pre-lane run 2026-09-04T17-21-07-726Z): probe walk 2283 vs deep walk 2306 — a 23-element/1.0% difference — first mismatch at walk index 311 (both tag 'div'; probe parent 292 vs deep parent 303, an 11-element offset in the animated hero card region q1lnWq_responseText / uPPvIq_cardWrap) discarded 1995 of 2306 nodes = 86.5%.
alignmentProvenance: PRE-EXISTING BY CONSTRUCTION — the Task 17 design as narrowed by the Task 26 revision. Present and identical (311/2306 = 13.5%) in EVERY run back to 2026-09-03T11-40-19-339Z including all four pre-lane runs, and already recorded verbatim in src/reconstruction/tree-switch.ts:701-709. The brief's '927 nodes / 40.2%' is the POST-lane desktop figure (1379/2306) and is load-to-load nondeterminism in linear's hero: the desktop column flips between 100% and 12-60% across runs with no code change between several of them.

collapse: NEW src/observer/navigate-document.ts — isOkStatus, navigateMainDocument and pause MOVED (not reimplemented) out of observe-page.ts into a module both load paths can depend on. layout-probe.ts cannot import observe-page.ts (observe-page.ts already imports autoScrollPrepare from layout-probe.ts), so a shared module is what makes ONE policy reachable from both loads.

src/observer/layout-probe.ts probeLayout — gate 1: navigateMainDocument replaces the bare page.goto, giving the probe the same non-2xx bounded retry the deep load has; the full documentResponse (every attempt + status) is written into the probe artifact.

src/observer/layout-probe.ts probeLayout — gate 2: a STARVATION gate, because a soft error page answers HTTP 200 and no status check can catch it. The probe compares its walk against the deep walk of the SAME viewport in the SAME run and, when starved, retries the whole probe from a clean browser CONTEXT (MAX_PROBE_ATTEMPTS=2), keeping the better pass.

src/observer/observe-page.ts — applyProbeIntegrity marks the viewport 'probe-starved'; the page-level roll-up was MOVED to after the probes run (it ran before them, so a starved probe could not have marked anything even if it had noticed). Marking, never dropping: the deep observation stays usable.
alignment: src/sitespec/compile-page.ts computeProbeAttachment — identity stops being a POSITION and becomes a STRUCTURAL PATH: each element's chain of tag[nth-of-that-tag-among-its-parent's-children] from the root, interned across both walks so comparison is an integer compare. Two elements correspond when their paths are equal — the same identity a CSS selector uses. An inserted node renames only its own later siblings; the rest of the document keeps its identity.

Conservative by construction: an element whose path differs attaches NOTHING (every later sibling of an inserted node, every descendant of a changed ancestor). A node either carries its own measurement or none, and can never carry someone else's.
attachProbeToViewport writes per MATCHED PAIR, since probe index and element index are no longer the same number.

A diff-with-resynchronization was implemented and measured FIRST, then rejected: it recovers the same coverage but must GUESS which side to skip at a divergence, and among identical siblings every choice satisfies tag-and-parent equally — guessing wrong shifts the tail by one sibling and attaches each node its neighbour's box, silently. Two candidate orderings were measured; each was correct on one synthetic fixture and silently wrong on the other. Path identity measured equal-or-better on all 172 real page/viewport probes.
fix.generic: No host, path, page or site is named anywhere in the fix. The starvation denominator is the run's own control (the same principle CROSS_VIEWPORT_STARVATION_RATIO already established), and PROBE_DOCUMENT_STARVATION_RATIO is DEFINED AS that existing constant rather than a second tuned number. With no denominator the probe reports no ratio rather than inventing one.

remainingRisk: The trigger is still out there: the fix converts a transient upstream error into a retry and, failing that, into a loud mark. It does not make linear.app's edge reliable. A run where BOTH probe attempts fail now yields a marked, refused probe — honest, but still no width evidence for that viewport.
MAX_PROBE_ATTEMPTS=2 costs a second full probe pass on a starved page (~90s on linear /). Bounded to one extra pass for that reason.

Path identity is stricter than a prefix in one direction: an element whose ancestry legitimately differs between the two loads now attaches nothing where a prefix might by luck have covered it. Measured cost across 172 real probes: none — every row equal or better.

The alignment floor is asserted in the SUITES, not enforced by the compiler — a page that genuinely changes between loads must still compile. The floor's job is to make a collapse fail loudly in a lane, which is where the last one got through.
